newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power seen higher before expiry on nuke news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power seen higher before expiry on nuke news.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Wednesday on output reduction at a Arizona nuclear power station, ahead of the July contracts' expiration market sources said.

In over-the-counter (OTC) business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $33.25-33.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) above Tuesday's settlement at $33.35 after traded as high as $34.50. July California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $20.50-21.00 versus yesterday's close at $20.86.
August OTC PV was discussed at $34.40-34.90 compared with Tuesday's settle at $34.85 and August OTC COB was quoted at $23.70-24.10 against yesterday's close at $23.90.

Electricity output at the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear power plant near Phoenix dropped to 60 percent of capacity from 100 percent early Wednesday due to a low pressure feedwater heater outage, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily status report.
The power complex is also supported by concerns over the restart of the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state, market sources said.
Restart of WNP-2 might be pushed back beyond expectations of later this week because it still requires Nuclear Regulatory Commission approval.
Meanwhile, Bonneville Power Administration, which markets WNP-2's power production, has said it hopes the unit will resume output late next week.
"There's no support as far as temperature goes," said a West Coast electricity broker.
Meteorologists called for temperatures in the Northwest to run below early summer norms through next week, while those in the Southwest would average mostly near to above normal.
